raw_comment: One thing I immediately took notice of the first time I looked over this graphic was the stark and surprising difference between the heat/droughts in arizona in comparison to states such as oklahoma and ohio. This observation led me to question why arizona, often nick-named the “convection oven of the United States” does not have more intense droughts? Could it have something to do with the fact that it is geographically closer to the coast? I can relate this back to my community because florida happens to be a state that is surrounded by ocean, as such it could be used as a good comparison point for potential issues that come with global warming and it could yield especially fascinating results as it is one of the only states that is almost entirely shielded from the effects of droughts yet still heavily affected by climate change. Moreover, if I were to give this graphic a headline, it would probably be “The Strike of Droughts, A study of Climate.”
